sources.citation: Jonathan L. Freedman, Scott C. Fraser (1966). Compliance without pressure: The foot-in-the-door technique. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology.
sources.notes: Foundational primary study (1966) in Journal of Personality and Social Psychology establishing the core experimental paradigm and quantitative parameters.

sources.citation: Patricia Pliner, Heather Hart, Joanne Kohl, Dory Saari (1974). Compliance without pressure: Some further data on the foot-in-the-door technique. Journal of Experimental Social Psychology.
sources.notes: Pliner, Hart, Kohl & Saari (1974) Cancer Society charity pin to donation field replication confirming self-perception commitment across real monetary giving.

sources.citation: Malgorzata Gamian-Wilk, Dariusz Dolinski (2020). The Foot-in-the-Door Phenomenon 40 and 50 Years Later: A Direct Replication of the Original Freedman and Fraser Study in Poland and in Ukraine. Psychological Reports.
sources.notes: Subsequent empirical and theoretical investigation (2020) in Psychological Reports extending the foundational findings.

sources.citation: Jerry M. Burger (1999). The Foot-in-the-Door Compliance Procedure: A Multiple-Process Analysis and Review. Personality and Social Psychology Review.
sources.notes: Burger (1999 Personality and Social Psychology Review) meta-analytic multiple-process review of foot-in-the-door self-perception, consistency, and extrinsic-payment moderators.

sources.citation: Janice G. Williams, Cecilia H. Solano (1983). The Social Reality of Feeling Lonely. Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin.
sources.notes: Beaman, Cole, Preston, Klentz & Steblay (1983 PSPB) quantitative meta-analysis across 15 years of foot-in-the-door field experiments.
